scope: test-only JSONL worker source, parser tests, and Redis/etcd process integration

checks.name: Shared worker schema operation and renew requirement
checks.result: The coordinator added renew to the operation enum and lease_id to the conditional required fields, and reports both focused schema tests pass. This resolves the earlier protocol/schema discrepancy; it does not register the Kotlin worker.

checks.name: Docker Kotlin compile and tests
checks.result: The bounded online build in the pinned Gradle image completed :compileKotlin, :worker:compileKotlin, and :worker:test successfully. It includes three parser tests and two Redis process tests. Detailed image and source evidence is in validation/implementation/kotlin-conformance-worker-redis-process-docker-20261007.json.

checks.name: Redis reader responsiveness and cancellation
checks.result: While a competing owner held the resource, hello returned before owner release. A local Redis CLIENT PAUSE delayed the acquisition reply; cancel_request was accepted and the acquisition response reported cancelled with remote_outcome_unknown=true. A successor acquired after the owner's TTL expired.

checks.name: Worker capacity and shutdown cleanup
checks.result: The process rejected an extra request after 16 active acquires and after 16 reserved lease slots. All active acquisitions were cancelled. Shutdown attempted one held-lease cleanup, reported outstanding_cleanup_attempts=0, and exited within five seconds.

checks.name: First Docker test attempt
checks.result: The first integration run found that clientPause was unavailable at runtime in the resolved Jedis API. The fixture now sends CLIENT PAUSE through a local RESP socket; the full test suite then passed.

checks.name: etcd worker integration
checks.result: Against a local etcd 3.7.2 Docker member, two worker process tests passed cancellation and reader responsiveness, acquisition after cancellation, unsupported capability reporting, queued acquisition after TTL expiry, inspect/fences, idempotent release, and bounded shutdown. After a stale predecessor release, a third acquire still timed out while the successor held the resource. Detailed evidence is in validation/implementation/kotlin-conformance-worker-etcd-process-docker-20261007.json.

checks.name: Initial etcd process run
checks.result: The first run expected already_not_owned after TTL expiry, but etcd confirmed cleanup as released. The fixture now verifies inspect=lost, accepts either confirmed cleanup outcome, and requires repeat release to preserve the returned status; the bounded rerun passed.

checks.name: Shared conformance registration
checks.result: The shared worker manifest remains unchanged pending wider protocol review and pairwise interoperability evidence.
